result.title: GuardianAgentFlow: Multi-Agent Coordination for Web Privacy Protection
result.summary: Web agents need to use private context without unnecessarily disclosing it. Effective protection must distinguish between requests that may be sent after sanitization and those that must be withheld, while preserving the information needed for authorized tasks. We present GuardianAgentFlow, a multi-agent framework that mediates outgoing Web requests through an explicit release contract. A dedicated restriction check grounds permission in the user's instruction; a shared protection scope aligns rewriting with disclosure checking; and candidate-grounded feedback guides revision before transmission. Experiments on Web requests with human-reviewed intent labels show improved request-contract success, while controlled comparisons and role ablations identify the contributions of restriction handling, policy evidence, and candidate checking. Evaluations of action proposals from PrivacyLens and AgentDAM demonstrate complementary protection when mediation is composed with privacy-aware agents. Experiments with smaller mediation models show that the coordination benefit persists with reduced model capacity. Dedicated-server measurements show lower mediation latency than full-policy reasoning, while real-site browser tests quantify integration overhead.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GuardianAgentFlow 多智能体框架，通过显式的「释放契约」对 Web 智能体发出的请求做中介：由限制检查将权限锚定在用户指令上，用共享保护范围对齐改写与披露核查，并以候选依据反馈在发送前引导修订。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「哪些信息可放行、哪些须保留」的门控与改写—复核循环，可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选、证据充分性判断与停止决策提供问题表述上的类比，可核查其限制检查和候选核查机制是否能迁移为 latent 内容的放行判据。
